title: Optimization of bimodal fitting
summary:
Many people with a cochlear implant (CI) wear a hearing aid on the other ear – this is called bimodal hearing. Together, both devices can significantly improve hearing ability. However, optimal alignment between the two systems is crucial – yet often difficult to achieve, as the CI is typically fitted in a clinic, while the hearing aid is adjusted by a hearing aid specialist. As a result, the two devices do not always work together ideally.
In this study, we want to investigate whether optimal alignment between the hearing aid and the CI processor improves hearing performance – particularly in terms of sound localization, speech understanding in noise, and subjective hearing experience.
Participants will be tested with three different combinations of hearing aid and CI processor:
1. Their own hearing aid and their own CI processor (current setup).
2. A new hearing aid and a new CI processor (new technology, but independently adjusted).
3. A new hearing aid and a new CI processor, optimally matched to each other (best possible combination).
In each configuration, participants’ sound localization, speech understanding, and subjective hearing experience will be measured.

interventions.name:
The aim of the study is to investigate whether an optimized alignment—regarding timing, loudness, and pitch—between the hearing aid (HA) and the cochlear implant (CI) speech processor (SP) leads to improvements in sound localization, speech understanding, and subjective perception.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Unilaterally implanted with a MED-EL C40+ or newer cochlear implant
Hearing aid user on the contralateral ear (bimodal user)
At least 6 months of experience with a bimodal system
Fluent in German language
Pure Tone Average (PTA) on the hearing aid ear of 80 dB HL or better
At least 30% speech understanding on the CI
No more than one deactivated CI electrode
FlexSoft/Flex28 electrodes with a minimum insertion angle of 560°
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of compliance with any inclusion criteria
cognitive impairments
